Ridgeline's cloud bill has been climbing for months and nobody can say with confidence which team or environment is actually responsible, because resources were never tagged consistently in the first place. This lab fixes that end to end -- a real tagging pass, a cost view grouped by those tags, a staged budget, and an anomaly alert.

Tagging comes first, because a grouping by tag is only as good as its coverage -- one untagged resource group becomes an Untagged bucket on every chart that follows. Each resource gets team, environment, and cost-center tags, the taxonomy Chapter five introduced, applied for real instead of left as a slide.

With tags in place, the cost analysis view groups daily spend by team instead of listing raw resource names -- checkout next to catalog next to fulfillment, answering who is actually spending instead of what merely exists. That view then gets pinned onto the same dashboard holding Chapter four's Grafana reliability panels, not left inside Cost Management where only Finance looks.

A budget alone only warns after the money is spent, so this one stages two thresholds: eighty percent of actual spend, and a separate forecasted alert at one hundred percent, days before the month closes. That staged pair is Chapter five's FinOps framework in practice -- Inform, before Optimize or Operate ever has to react to a surprise.

On top of the budget sits an anomaly alert, scoped to the production resource group, comparing spend against Ridgeline's own recent pattern instead of a fixed number. That's the real gap a budget alone leaves open -- an anomaly alert catches a spike while it's still small, not thirty days later on an invoice.

Ridgeline now has a real cost dashboard pinned next to its reliability dashboard, a staged budget, and an anomaly alert -- cost finally gets caught as early as a reliability problem does, instead of showing up as a surprise on next month's invoice. Lesson 31 shows what happens when that shared visibility doesn't exist yet, and a cost-cutting decision gets made without anyone checking its reliability blast radius first.
